newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.17 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.17 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares firmed on last minute buying on Friday as traders took advantage of delayed payments ahead of a five-day new year holiday, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed the year at a new all-time high of 97,588.81, up 163.20 points, or 0.17 percent from Thursday's previous record of 97,425.62.
The stock market will be closed until January 2. Yesterday's deals will be settled next Thursday and today's next Friday.
In dollar terms, the index stood at 91 cents, unchanged from Thursday, but down from a $1 record on April 8.
The market index surged 143.8 percent from last year's close of 40,024.57. In dollar terms, the rise was 35.8 percent from the end-1995 close of $0.67.
Brokers said trade was quiet due to weak volume which dived to 11.40 trillion lira ($106.1 million) from Thurday's 14.85 trillion ($138.6 million).
"Trade was unexpectedly dull for the year's last session, but some buying emerged towards the close to push the index above the 97,000 level," said Erol Guney from Yurtbank.

The government on Thursday extended the holiday to five days to January 2 by declaring December 30 and 31 official holiday in the public sector. The Exchange afterwards said the market would also be closed on Monday and Tuesday.
The market index rose 3.32 percent this week after a 6.2 percent surge last week.
